meta.title: EU Cloud Sovereignty Framework — Sovereignty Calculator

frontSheet: Please note: column E "score" has been filled with fictitious values that do not refer to any specific example for the sole purpose of exemplification. — the source calculator's own note. The estate named "Source worked example" reproduces those fictitious selections, so it demonstrates the instrument and measures nobody.

Seven rows of the source carry a SEAL tag with no readable text (rows 7, 17, 31, 33, 38, 48, 49). A choice nobody can read is not a choice, so they are not imported: 233 rungs, not 240. Nothing else was changed, repaired or reworded.

Five questions — SOV-3.5, SOV-5.1, SOV-5.2, SOV-5.3 and SOV-6.5 — score but never gate. That is the source's own published remedy (Implementation Guidance, Lessons learnt, p13): "The level SEAL-4 … is not achievable today in the context of EU Sovereignty considering existing dependencies to specific supply chains (chips, hardware). Relaxing level SEAL-4, at least temporarily, would allow to make more difference between providers." The rungs keep their honest SEAL tags; the five questions simply stop feeding the floor.

sealLevels.name: No Sovereignty
sealLevels.description: No sovereign control; fully dependent on a foreign-controlled provider.

sealLevels.name: Jurisdictional Sovereignty
sealLevels.description: Operated under EU jurisdiction, but control can still be overridden from outside.

sealLevels.name: Data Sovereignty
sealLevels.description: The EU controls the data even under stress; outside parties cannot compel access.

sealLevels.name: Technological Sovereignty
sealLevels.description: The EU controls the technology and can keep operating if a foreign supplier withdraws.

sealLevels.name: Full Digital Sovereignty
sealLevels.description: Complete sovereign control across law, data, and technology, down to the supply chain.

roles.name: Assessment team
roles.description: The whole room. The source calculator splits its questions across no roles, so one role carries all 48.

parties.name: Assessed organisation
parties.description: The organisation the calculator is filled in about. The source names no supply-chain parties, so the taxonomy has exactly one type.

objectives.name: SOV-1 Strategic Sovereignty
objectives.description: Strategic sovereignty captures the degree to which a cloud provider (or technology actor) is anchored within the European Union/EEA legal, financial, and industrial ecosystem. It assesses ownership stability, governance influence, and alignment with EU strategic priorities.

questions.why: ensuring that ultimate decision-making authority resides within EU jurisdiction.

ladder.description: Entirely outside the EU
Mostly outside the EU
Mostly within the EU
Entirely within the EU

questions.why: evaluating the likelihood of takeover or transfer to non-sovereign owners

ladder.description: Very likely
Likely takeover by or transfer to a non-EU sovereign entity
Somewhat likely takeover by or transfer to a non-EU sovereign entity
Unlikely takeover by or transfer to a non-EU sovereign entity
Very unlikely

questions.why: measuring the capacity of EU stakeholders to shape the provider’s technological and service evolution.

ladder.description: No influence possible
Through "voice of the customer" public channels (e.g. feedback portals, online communities)
Governance bodies exist with EU actors participation
Full influence of EU actors

questions.why: degree to which the provider relies on EU-based financing rather than external capital.

ladder.description: Almost entirely relying on non-EU funding
Mostly relying on non-EU funding
Balanced mix of EU and non-EU funding
Majority of funding is EU-based
Entirely EU-based funding

questions.why: extent of investment, jobs, and value creation within EU/EEA.

ladder.description: Minimal
Some
Balanced EU/non-EU
Majority in the EU
Fully in the EU

questions.why: involvement in initiatives such as IPCEI-CIS, Horizon Europe, or Gaia-X.

ladder.description: No clear participation
Active participant in strategic projects
Strategic projects depend on contractor's involvement

questions.why: consistency with digital, green, and industrial sovereignty objectives defined at EU level.

ladder.description: No evidence exist
Existing Action plan (how to measure ambition? Through means linked to the goals? Relative to the size of the company?)
Already measured achievement and existing dedicated governance
Bold ambition and dedicated means

questions.why: ability to sustain secure operations even if vendor support is withdrawn or disrupted.

ladder.description: Immediate shutdown of the service is expected
Service would likely stop but with a delay to provide time for customer reaction
Can continue temporarily based on contractual agreement with EC
Ability to source alternative suppliers or internalise key functions
Full autonomy and continuity

objectives.name: SOV-2 Legal & Jurisdictional Sovereignty
objectives.description: Legal & Jurisdictional sovereignty evaluates the legal environment, exposure to foreign authority, and enforceability of rights that govern a technology provider and its services. It determines the extent to which a provider is anchored in European jurisdiction and insulated from external legal claims.

questions.why: the national legal system governing the provider’s operations and contracts.

ladder.description: Non-EU only
Mixed EU/non-EU
Exclusively EU law

questions.why: degree of exposure to non-EU laws with cross-border reach (all).

ladder.description: Fully exposed to non-EU laws
Mitigation clauses, exposure remains
EU subsidiary with contractual protections
Legal structures shielding from foreign law
Verified legal immunity, non-EU laws unenforceable

questions.why: existence of legal, contractual, or technical channels through which non-EU authorities could compel access to data or systems.

ladder.description: Non-EU authorities can compel access to data or systems without customers being notified
Non-EU authorities can compel access to data or systems without customers being notified, in specific cases
Non-EU authorities can compel access to data or systems with customers being notified in all cases
Non-EU authorities requests to access data or systems are disputed by the provider and eventually in some cases are accepted with customers being notified
Non-EU authorities requests to access data or systems are always rejected by the provider

questions.why: applicability of international regimes such as ITAR or EAR, which may restrict usage or transfer.

ladder.description: Restrictions exists towards a EU MS
Restrictions exists towards EU citizens or international organisations
Share of revenues >50% in the EU
Part of the offer cannot be exposed to restrictions towards EU MSs
Part of the offer cannot be exposed to restrictions towards EU MSs or international organisations

questions.why: location of intellectual property creation, registration, and development (all).

ladder.description: Entirely outside the EU
Mostly outside the EU
Mixed within/outside the EU
Mostly within the EU
Fully within the EU

questions.why: legal jurisdiction where IP rights are owned and enforced.

ladder.description: non-EU law, one single country
non-EU law, mixed non-EU countries
Mixed law, some EU
EU law with exceptions
fully under EU law

objectives.name: SOV-3 Data & AI Sovereignty
objectives.description: Data & AI sovereignty focuses on the protection, control, and independence of data assets and AI services within the EU/EEA. It addresses how data is secured, where it is processed, and the degree of autonomy customers retain over AI   capabilities.

ladder.description: Provider only
Primarily the provider but not exclusively
Shared - provider has override keys
Customer primary control but provider can read the data or some of the data
Customer exclusive control - provider can not read the data

questions.why: visibility into when, where, and by whom data is accessed, including auditability of AI model usage.

ladder.description: No data usage logs
Basic logs incomplete (missing date; missing user; missing type of access; missing means of access etc.)
Logs exist but not real-time or controlled by vendor (vendor is replaced by CUSTOMER in the survey)
Full customer controlled visibility of log access but not in real time
Real-time customer oversight and independent auditability

questions.text: Secure deletion & proof of erasure od data
questions.why: mechanisms guaranteeing irreversible removal of data, with verifiable evidence.

ladder.description: No, irreversible deletion is neither guaranteed nor verifiable
Manual confirmation only
Internal validation based on policies - no proof of validation left
Deletion is technically verified with access logs
Yes, irreversible deletion is systematically enforced and independently verified

questions.why: strict confinement of storage and processing to European jurisdictions, with no fallback to third countries.

ladder.description: Data location largely unknown and includes third countries without controls
Data partly in the EU, significant reliance on third countries and limited control
Data mainly in the EU, some third-country use with standard safeguards
Data in the EU by default, tightly controlled exceptions
All data exclusively in the EU with no third-country fallback

questions.why: extent to which AI models and data pipelines are developed, trained, hosted, and governed under EU control, minimizing dependence on non-EU technology stacks.

ladder.description: Non-EU or undetermined: Black-box AI, restricted chips
Mostly non-EU dependencies: Licensed AI, chip dependency
Mixed Control with alternatives: Auditable or open source AI, foreign chips
EU-led AI, foreign accelerators
EU-origin models and chips - no dependencies from outside EU

objectives.name: SOV-4 Operational Sovereignty
objectives.description: Operational sovereignty measures the practical ability of EU actors to run, support, and evolve a technology independently of foreign control. It focuses on continuity of operations, skill availability, and resilience against external dependencies.

questions.why: ease of migrating workloads or integrating with alternative EU-controlled solutions without vendor lock-in.

ladder.description: No guarantees are provided for data or workload portability
Data export and workload portability is provided on a "best-effort" basis
Standard documented methods for data export are available
Formal migration services are available to assist with moving data and workloads
Solution already deployed on sovereign infrastructure

questions.text: Ability to Operate Without Foreign Dependencies
questions.why: capacity for EU operators to manage, maintain, and support the technology without requiring non-EU vendor involvement

ladder.description: Critical operational services are delivered by non-EU teams
Operational services are partially sourced from within the EU
Operational responsibilities are balanced between EU and non-EU teams
Operational services are predominantly delivered by EU-based teams
The entire technology stack is managed and supported by a fully EU-based team

questions.text: Skill Availability- existence of an EU-based talent pool with the expertise to operate and sustain the service.

ladder.description: Global team, mainly non-EU
Mixed, majority outside EU
Majority EU, escalation abroad
All EU staff
100% EU staff + clearance

questions.why: assurance that operational support is delivered from within the EU and subject exclusively to EU/EEA legal frameworks

ladder.description: The support team is global with the majority of staff located outside the EU
The team is mixed but the majority of support staff reside outside the EU
The majority of support staff are in the EU but escalations are handled by non-EU teams
All support staff are located within the EU
All support staff are located within the EU and hold relevant security clearances

questions.why: availability of full technical documentation, source code, and operational know-how enabling long-term autonomy.

ladder.description: Global/non-EU exposure - Documentation/knowledge is stored or managed outside EU and may be subject to non-EU jurisdiction or access
EU optional, not enforced - EU storage is available as an option, but it is not enforced
EU primary with non-EU fallback - Stored/managed in the EU by default, but some storage/replication/access outside the EU may occur (e.g., disaster recovery/support)
EU-only primary repositories - All primary documentation and knowledge repositories are stored in the EU (no routine non-EU storage/processing)
EU-only end-to-end - Content, metadata, and backups/replicas are stored in the EU and privileged administration/support access is restricted to EU-based staff under EU jurisdiction

questions.why: location and legal control of critical suppliers or subcontractors involved in service delivery.

ladder.description: Immediate shutdown of the service is expected
Service would likely stop but with a delay to provide time for customer reaction
Can continue temporarily based on contractual agreement with EC
Ability to source alternative suppliers or internalise key functions
Full autonomy and continuity

objectives.name: SOV-5 Supply Chain Sovereignty
objectives.description: Supply chain sovereignty evaluates the geographic origin, transparency, and resilience of the technology supply chain, focusing on the extent to which critical components and processes remain under EU control   or exposed to non-EU dependencies.

questions.why: geographic source of key physical parts

ladder.description: No disclosure
Partial disclosure
Transparent with exceptions
Full transparency
EU-certified provenance

questions.why: countries where hardware is manufactured or assembled

ladder.description: Fully foreign, black box
Foreign origin, partial disclosure
Mixed sourcing, EU audit rights
Build by EU Teams, on the basis of a foreign code
Exclusive designed and build by EU Teams

questions.why: jurisdiction and provenance of embedded code controlling hardware, firmwares

ladder.description: No disclosure
Partial disclosure
Transparent with exceptions
Full transparency
EU-certified provenance

questions.why: where and by whom software is architected and programmed

ladder.description: Software is of fully foreign origin with no transparency ('black box')
Software is of foreign origin with partial disclosure on its development
Core and essential parts of the software are designed and maintained by EU teams
A large majority of the software is designed and maintained by EU teams
The software is exclusively designed and maintained by EU teams

questions.why: location and jurisdiction governing software packaging, distribution, and updates.

ladder.description: Non-EU control & execution - Build/release/deployment is executed and governed by non-EU teams, with pipeline control and approvals under non-EU jurisdiction
EU control, non-EU execution - Execution is performed by non-EU teams, but pipeline administration and final release approvals are under EU jurisdiction
Non-EU control, EU execution - Execution is performed by EU teams, but pipeline administration and/or final release approvals (incl. signing) are under non-EU jurisdiction
EU control & execution - Build/release/deployment is executed by EU teams and governed from within the EU (pipeline administration, signing, approvals)

EU control and EU policy gates - As (4), plus EU-based compliance/security gates enforced in the pipeline (e.g., signing under your control, vulnerability checks, segregation of duties, auditable approvals)

questions.why: degree of reliance on non-EU vendors, facilities, or proprietary technologies

ladder.description: Only non-EU vendors or facilities involved
Mostly non-EU vendors or facilities involved in critical services, non documented
Few non-EU vendors or facilities involved in critical services, non documented, or non-EU vendors/facilities transparently documented
Few non-EU vendors or facilities involved in non-critical services, documented
No depedency on non-EU vendor or facility

questions.why: visibility into the entire supplier and sub-supplier chain, including audit rights.

ladder.description: No suppliers can be audited
Some suppliers and subcontractors can be audited
Critical suppliers and subcontractors can be audited
Most suppliers and subcontractors can be audited
All suppliers and subcontractors can be audited

objectives.name: SOV-6 Technology Sovereignty
objectives.description: Technology sovereignty evaluates the degree of openness, transparency, and independence in the underlying technological stack, ensuring EU actors can interoperate, audit, and evolve solutions without lock-in to foreign proprietary systems.

questions.why: ability to integrate with other technologies through well-documented and non-proprietary APIs or protocols.

ladder.description: Closed proprietary interfaces - Integrations rely on closed or proprietary interfaces and formats controlled by the vendor
Restricted proprietary APIs - Some vendor APIs exist, but they are limited/restricted (access, scope, licensing) and interoperability remains vendor-controlled
Mixed (partial openness) - Key interfaces are documented and partly standards-based, but important functions or data formats remain proprietary/vendor-specific

Standards-based and broadly compatible - Interfaces and data formats predominantly follow recognised open standards (e.g., ETSI/CEN/CENELEC, ISO/IEC, IETF/W3C) with stable versioning and full documentation

Open-by-default with portability - All critical functions are accessible via open, well-documented, non-proprietary APIs and standard formats, with published specifications and minimal vendor-specific dependencies enabling easy third-party integration

questions.why: extent to which the solution adheres to publicly governed and widely adopted standards, reducing dependency on single vendors

ladder.description: No open standards - Core services (e.g., identity and access management, data formats, messaging, security, logging, integration protocols) rely mainly on proprietary technologies
Ad hoc use - Open standards are used inconsistently on a case-by-case basis, without documented rationale or governance
Partial core adoption - Open standards are used and documented for some core services, while other core services remain proprietary/vendor-specific
Policy for most core services - A formal policy mandates and documents open standards for most core services, with managed exceptions
Policy for all core services - A formal policy mandates and documents open standards for all core services

questions.why: whether software is accessible under open licenses, with rights to audit, modify, and redistribute, ensuring transparency and adaptability

ladder.description: The software is fully closed-source with no rights to audit or modify and its governance is vendor-controlled
Source code is available for review but modification and handover rights are under very strict conditions
The software is open source , permitting modification and redistribution, but governance is centralised (e.g., single-company or non-open foundation), limiting strategic autonomy or smooth handover
The software is open source with significant EU contributions but governance is restricted and handover is possible
Fully open-source software is governed by an independent or EU-based entity, granting full rights to audit, modify, redistribute, and seamlessly transfer stewardship

questions.why: visibility into the design and functioning of the service, including architectural documentation, data flows, and dependencies

ladder.description: No insight provided
Insight accessible during audits
Some public insight exists (all)
Large corpus of public insight exists (all)
Customers can contribute to adapt and enhance the service

questions.why: degree of European independence in high-performance computing capabilities, including processors, accelerators, and software ecosystems.

ladder.description: Imported black-box HPC computers
EU-hosted, foreign stack
Co-designed or integrated in EU
EU processor IP, non-EU fabs
EU design + EU fab + EU ops

objectives.name: SOV-7 Security & Compliance Sovereignty
objectives.description: Security & Compliance sovereignty measures the extent to which security operations, compliance obligations, and resilience measures are controlled within the EU  , ensuring independence from foreign jurisdictions and long-term operational assurance.

questions.why: attainment of EU and internationally recognized certifications (all)

ladder.description: ELA0
ELA1
EAL2
ELA3
EAL4-5

questions.why: demonstrable adherence to GDPR, NIS2, DORA, and other EU frameworks

ladder.description: No evident adherence to any EU Regulations
Limited compliance to some well-known EU Regulations (basic practices exist but informal, incomplete, or non-systematic)
Moderate compliance to some well-know EU Regulations (controls exist but gaps remain; compliance not fully demonstrated)
Partial compliance to most of the well-known EU Regulations (requirements implemented and operational with minor exceptions)
Fully compliant to all well-know EU regulations (verified compliance, independently audited)

questions.why: security operations centers and response teams operating exclusively under EU jurisdiction.

ladder.description: The SOC and incident response teams are located outside the EU
A hybrid model is used with SOC functions split between EU and non-EU locations
The primary SOC is in the EU but incidents may be escalated to non-EU teams
The entire incident lifecycle is handled by teams operating exclusively within the EU. Threat intelligence and incident data obtained mostly via EU sources
The full incident lifecycle is handled by EU-based teams with active participation in ENISA's information sharing frameworks. Threat intelligence and incident data are gathered worldwide

questions.why: customer or EU authority ability to oversee logs, alerts, and monitoring functions directly.

ladder.description: The provider retains full control over all security logs and monitoring
Customers receive periodic reports based on security logs
Customers have access to a basic portal for monitoring
Customers have full direct access to their security monitoring and logs which are stored in the EU
Customers have full access to immutable tamper-proof logs stored exclusively within the EU

questions.why: transparent, timely, and EU-compliant reporting of breaches or vulnerabilities

ladder.description: No compliance - ad-hoc or absent breach reporting workflow, with no possibility to collaborate with EU CSIRTs or to support EU-led investigations
Limited compliance - reporting is reactive with limited transparency and unguaranteed timelines;  CSIRT cooperation possible on best-effort basis
Moderate compliance - GDPR/NIS2-aligned reporting procedures in place with vulnerabilities and breaches communicated within mandated timelines; CSIRT cooperation available but not real-time

Partial compliance - there is a monitored reporting flow with internal SLAs equal or below regulatory maximums; contractually prepared to support EU-directed investigations; data sharing with EU CSIRTs available but not in real-time

Full compliance - full EU-compliant breach disclosure with real-time data sharing to EU CSIRTs with audit-backed processes, proactive vulnerability disclosure and threat intel sharing; proven readiness for investigations

questions.why: ability to develop, test, and apply security patches independently of non-EU vendors

ladder.description: No autonomy in the deployment of security patches
Limited Autonomy - security patches are deployed according to vendor schedules; basic testing is possible
Moderate Autonomy - security patches are deployed with sufficient notice to the customer and testing is possible, except for zero-day patching
High Autonomy - security patches can be deployed independently by the customer, without customers' checks
Full Autonomy - security patches can be deployed independently by the customer, with customers' checks

questions.why: capacity for EU entities to perform independent security and compliance audits with full access.

ladder.description: No access to entities other than the vendor
Limited access to independent entities to the data provided by the vendor
Partial control by independent entities on the data provided by the vendor
High control by independent entities to request data from the vendor
Full control by any idependent entity to perform security and compliance audits

objectives.name: SOV-8 Environmental Sustainability
objectives.description: Environmental sustainability assesses autonomy and resilience of cloud services over the long term in relation to energy usage, dependency and raw material scarcity.

questions.why: adoption of energy-efficient infrastructure (all) and measurable improvement targets.

ladder.description: PUE > 0
PUE < 3
PUE < 1.5 + roadmap
PUE < 1.3
PUE < 1.2 EU verified

questions.why: circular economy practices ensuring reuse, refurbishment, and responsible end-of-life treatment of hardware.

ladder.description: No policy
Circular economy EU-aligned
Documented program
Circular economy EU-aligned
EU-certified lifecycle

questions.why: transparent measurement and disclosure of carbon emissions, water usage, and other sustainability indicators.

ladder.description: No reporting
Detailed EU methodology
Annual report
Detailed EU methodology
EU-audited reporting

questions.why: sourcing of renewable or low-carbon energy to power infrastructure and operations

ladder.description: Non traceable
Only EU energy supplies
Mix of EU and non-EU supplies
Only EU energy supplies
Only green EU energy supplies

testEstates.name: Source worked example
testEstates.description: The 47 selections the source spreadsheet ships in column E, reproduced rung for rung. SOV-1.6 is left unanswered because the source leaves it blank. The source itself calls these values fictitious, so this estate demonstrates the instrument and measures nobody.

testEstates.name: Best available today
testEstates.description: A ceiling probe, not a claim about any vendor: a hypothetical fully-European provider that takes the top rung everywhere except the five silicon questions, where it takes choice-4, the second-from-top rung. It exists to answer one question — is SEAL-4 reachable at all?

answers.evidence: The source spreadsheet leaves this blank; nothing in this estate documents participation in an EU strategic programme.
